title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — imputation when not yet separate persons; reckoned as one man in Adam
pass_a_gloss: Therefore the imputation was made when we were not yet separate persons from Adam—or, in the interlocutor's phrase, when God considered us as one man in Adam. Placeus thinks the reader can now see for himself what force his earlier omnes argument has.
pass_b_english: That imputation was therefore made when we were not yet persons separate and distant from Adam—or, as the one I was dealing with puts it, when we were considered by God as one man in Adam. Now, I think, you yourself, reader, sufficiently see what force the argument has.
source_text: Facta est igitur ista imputatio cum nondum essemus personae separatae & distantes ab Adamo: vel, ut loquitur is quicum mihi res erat, cum consideraremus a Deo tanquam unus homo in Adamo. Nunc, opinor, quam vim habeat argumentum, ipse per te, Lector, satis intelligis.

choices.choice: Imputed when not yet separate; one man in Adam
